newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian govt in deal with opposition over tv bill.
newsitem.headline: Italian govt in deal with opposition over tv bill.

text.p: Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government struck a deal on Monday with the centre-right opposition over measures for the broadcasting sector which will replace three decrees due to expire at the end of the year.
The measures, contained in a single jumbo package, will now go before parliament for approval.
One of the expiring decrees allowed opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi's Mediaset company to carry on broadcasting its three terrestrial tv channels until the end of January.

Under the terms of Monday's deal, the government has agreed to extend Mediaset's licences until the end of next May, said Mario Landolfi, the head of information at the hard-right National Alliance party.
This extension could be renewed further if the bill is approved in at least one of Italy's two houses of parliament before the end of the May deadline, Landolfi said.
The Constitutional Court ruled two years ago that no single proprietor should be allowed to keep three TV channels and set August 1996 as the deadline for changes to be implemented.

The government extended current ownership rules until the end of January 1997 after that deadline passed in order to plug a legal gap in which magistrates could technically have forced Berlusconi to take one of his channels off the air.
The government welcomed Monday's agreement, but Prodi said he was determined to get the package ratified by parliament by the next March.
Post and Communictions Minister Antonio Maccanico, who negotiated the deal, said the accord should help defuse political tension in Italy.
"This is a good deal which has tackled and sought to resolve a string of serious problems which are blocking Italian parliamentary life," he said.
The opposition and government have clashed heavily in recent months, with Prodi resorting to numerous do-or-die confidence votes to blast legislation passed by opposition filibustering.
